name: Cicada 3301
title: A Plastic Duck, a Phone Number, and the Number 3301
claims: Cicada 3301 is the name for three sets of puzzles posted online under the name "3301" between 2012 and 2014 | 1
The first puzzle started January 4, 2012 on 4chan and ran for nearly a month | 1
A second round began January 4, 2013; a third was posted on Twitter January 4, 2014 | 1
The third puzzle remains unsolved | 1
A new clue was posted on Twitter on January 5, 2016 | 1
The last verified OpenPGP-signed message came in April 2017, denying the validity of any unsigned puzzle | 1
The stated intent was to recruit "intelligent individuals" | 1
Puzzles focused on data security, cryptography, steganography, internet anonymity | 1
The Washington Post listed it among the top 5 eeriest unsolved mysteries of the internet; it has been called "the most elaborate and mysterious puzzle of the Internet age" | 1
Speculation includes NSA, CIA, MI6, Mossad, a "Masonic conspiracy", a cyber mercenary group | 1
Others say it is an alternate reality game, though no company or individual has tried to monetize it | 1
Theories include a secret society to improve cryptography, privacy and anonymity, or a cult or religion | 1
Several 2012 solvers said 3301 typically uses non-puzzle recruiting but created the puzzles to find people with cryptography and computer security skills | 1

A 2013 solver said solvers were asked about support for information freedom, online privacy and freedom, and rejection of censorship; satisfactory answers led to a private forum and a project to further the group's ideals | 1
That solver did not finish their work on a method of general decryption and the website was removed | 1

A fellow winner documented the experience in a YouTube series described as a "more realistic, fact based view of the organization" and now facilitates community efforts on a Discord server; other solver communities remain on message boards and forums | 1
Clues included digital images with hidden information, a telephone message, websites, paper signs with QR codes | 1
Solvers met cryptographic and steganographic techniques and references to literature, poetry, art and music | 1
Each clue was signed by the same OpenPGP private key | 1
Agrippa, a poem from the Mabinogion, and The Book of the Law were used in the puzzle | 1
In 2012 Chile's Investigative Police (PDI) claimed Cicada 3301 was a hacker group engaged in illegal activities; Cicada issued a PGP-signed denial | 1

In July 2015 a group calling itself "3301" hacked Planned Parenthood's database; Cicada issued a signed statement saying it was not associated and did not condone use of its name, number or symbolism; the hacker group later confirmed no affiliation | 1
The US Navy released a cryptographic challenge based on the puzzles in 2014, called Project Architeuthis | 1

The 2015 Person of Interest episode "Nautilus" featured a similar worldwide cryptographic game with a nautilus shell; its creator said Cicada 3301 was the inspiration and called it "a very interesting concept out there" | 1
The 2021 film Dark Web: Cicada 3301 was directed by Alan Ritchson | 1
4chan is anonymous, requires no registration, has no formal archive, and most posts expire or are deleted within hours | 2
Some commenters on the board suggested the message might be an NSA recruiting exercise | 2
An early solver was told to open the image in WordPad and found text at the bottom: TIBERIVS CLAVDIVS CAESAR says followed by a garbled string | 2
Tiberius Claudius was the fourth Roman emperor; shifting the text back four letters (Caesar cipher) revealed a URL | 2
The URL showed a plastic duck image with "WOOPS just decoys this way. Looks like you can't guess how to get the message out." | 2
Someone linked "guess" and "out" to the software OutGuess, which extracted a link to a subreddit | 2
The subreddit showed Mayan numerals, lines of garbled letters, and two images labeled "welcome" and "problems?" | 2
Someone posted a link to an anonymous chat room on Mibbit; the solver said it started to feel a bit creepy and noted most trolls don't put this much energy in | 2
The solver worked through book codes, King Arthur and the Holy Grail clues on index cards and found a message beginning "call us on us tele phone number" | 2
The solver was doubted in the chat room, then received a private message "You're way ahead of the others" and an invitation to a private chat | 2
A recording said three primes were associated with the original final image, 3301 is one, find the other two, multiply them and add .com | 2
The first image's pixel dimensions were 509 and 503, both prime | 2

The resulting site showed a cicada image with a three-day countdown; OutGuess revealed "You have done well to come this far. Patience is a virtue. Check back at 17:00 on Monday, 9 January 2012. UTC." | 2
The solver reached this point around 2 a.m. | 2
Physical paper signs of the 2012 puzzle were found in Paris, Warsaw, Miami and Erskineville, a suburb of Sydney (Wikipedia figure: Locations of the physical paper signs from the 2012 puzzle) | 1
